title: What would make an optical signal trustworthy?
description: The available summary describes feasibility and design work around photonic glucose sensing. It does not provide a validated device result, clinical study or performance numbers suitable for a claim of measurement accuracy.
lead: The available summary describes feasibility and design work around photonic glucose sensing. It does not provide a validated device result, clinical study or performance numbers suitable for a claim of measurement accuracy.

sections.heading: What the supplied work supports
body: Research considered optical approaches and chip design for a sensing path. That supports explaining a physical hypothesis and design direction. It does not by itself establish selectivity, repeatability or performance in a complete device.

sections.heading: What remains to be shown
body: A convincing evaluation would specify sample conditions, reference measurements, calibration protocol, confounders and independent repeats. It would report both successes and failures across a defined range, with uncertainty and the conditions under which a result holds.

sections.heading: Next validation gate
body: The practical next gate is a documented prototype-and-measurement plan: build or integrate the relevant optical path, collect paired reference data, and test whether the response survives real variation. No numeric target is asserted here without an approved source.
